issue_text: "--notes" option ignores note tags that are entirely punctuation. Running `pylint test.py --notes="YES,???"` on a file with two fixme-style comments (`# YES: yes` and `# ???: no`) only reports W0511 for the first; the all-punctuation tag `???` is silently dropped. Expected: both should fire.
summary: The agent fixes a pylint false-negative where --notes silently drops note tags made entirely of punctuation (e.g. ???) — only alphanumeric tags fire W0511. The 13-turn run falls into three clean phases. Reproduce (T1–T3) builds the minimal two-line repro directly from the issue text and confirms only one W0511 fires. Localize (T4–T9) loses two turns to a recovery loop when grep interprets --notes as a flag (T5–T6), then walks into pylint/checkers/misc.py via match-count ranking and scrolling, reaching the bug at lines 124–126: a \b word-boundary assertion cannot anchor between two non-word characters, so ??? never matches. Edit and verify (T10–T13) replaces \b with a positive lookahead, re-runs the original repro, and confirms both tags fire before submitting. Verification is genuine — the exact command that failed at T3 succeeds at T11 — so the resolution is not circular. T9 is the cognitive peak of the run, with five distinct codebook moves in a single thought paragraph.

findings.title: T9 fires five groups in one paragraph
findings.body: Turn 9's thought spans Analysing, Retrieval, Inferring (twice: dataflow then diagnosis), and Planning — four subgroups in one unbroken paragraph. Whole-thought tagging collapses this into a single "Reasoning" label and loses the localize-to-edit pivot that Planning › Plan deeper inspection before edit captures.

findings.title: Recovery lives in one clause
findings.body: At T6, "use a different search term" is the entire signal that separates genuine recovery (Deciding › Pick alternative strategy) from the repeated mistake at T5. Without quote-level grounding, the two turns look identical.

findings.title: Sense groups cluster at phase boundaries
findings.body: Retrieval and Memory tags appear almost exclusively at the starts of phases — T2 reads the issue, T8 tracks the file cursor, T9 reads code semantics — while Think and Act dominate mid-phase turns. This boundary pattern is invisible at the turn level.

It seems that the issue might be related to how the regular expression is constructed or how it is used to match comments in the source code. The regular expression is built from the notes configuration, which is a list of comma-separated values, and an optional notes-rgx regular expression. The pattern is then compiled and used in the process_tokens method to search for matching comments. The issue might be that the regular expression pattern does not account for note tags that consist entirely of punctuation characters. turns.headline: Replace \b with a lookahead assertion.
turns.obs: File viewer centered on lines 122–128. The two \b occurrences at 124 and 126 are visible.
turns.thought: We are now looking at the section of the misc.py file where the regular expression for the --notes option is constructed. The regular expression is built from the notes configuration option, which is a list of note tags. These tags are escaped using re.escape and joined with a pipe | to form an alternation pattern. This pattern is then used to create a regular expression that matches comments starting with one of the note tags followed by a word boundary \b. The issue might be with the word boundary \b, which does not match if the tag is followed by punctuation. Since the tag "???" is entirely punctuation, the word boundary may not be recognized correctly, causing the tag not to match. To fix this issue, we can modify the regular expression to ensure that it matches note tags that are entirely punctuation. We can do this by removing the word boundary and allowing the tag to be followed by any non-word character or the end of the string. Let's edit the regular expression construction to fix the issue.

        regex_string = rf"#\s*({notes}|{self.config.notes_rgx})(?=\W|$)"

        regex_string = rf"#\s*({notes})(?=\W|$)"
end_of_edit
